title: Diplomacy press reject (engine -> sender)
description:
One refused press message of the sender's own batch. Per-message and deterministic: other messages of the batch are unaffected. Delivered to the sender only, in `press_rejects` of its NEXT observation (every transport; over `ws` the arena does not send a separate frame). A rejected message is never delivered, never enters the transcript, and IS counted for shared.budget_violation. `hint` is fixed platform text per code and never echoes the rejected content. Frame-level problems (unparseable JSON, schema_invalid, too_large, bad_echo) are not press rejects: they refuse the whole frame (errors.md §3a) and are counted in the EpisodeResult budget.

Exactly one code per rejected message: the FIRST failing check, in this fixed order: press_not_in_round, press_too_large, press_invalid_text, press_bad_recipient, reply_to_unknown, asks_invalid, terms_invalid | clause_beyond_horizon, offer_unknown | offer_self_accept | commitment_unknown, offer_conflict, signature_invalid, press_quota. Quota is checked last and is consumed only by messages that pass every other check, in batch order. (2.5.0) `terms_invalid` and `clause_beyond_horizon` share one position: the terms are checked clause by clause (give, then want); within a clause the phase-range rules come first (`terms_invalid`), then the horizon (`clause_beyond_horizon`), then the clause's other fields (`terms_invalid`). The first failing clause decides the code.

Codes:
- `press_too_large`: oversize: a body over 2048 raw bytes, or over 600 bytes after sanitisation (200 for an offer-move body or terms.note). Rejected, never truncated.
- `press_invalid_text`: a body or note is empty after sanitisation, or contains a code point outside L*, N*, P*, S*, Zs; or terms.note is not already in sanitised form.
- `press_quota`: too many: over the tier quota (messages per round, messages or body bytes per movement window, broadcasts per window, or live offers). The first messages that fit are accepted in batch order.
- `press_not_in_round`: press sent in a step that is not a press round (intent, orders, retreat or adjustment). No press exists outside rounds r1..rR of a movement phase.
- `press_bad_recipient`: a recipient is eliminated, or the group size is invalid (the schema already rejects self-addressing).
- `signature_invalid`: offer, counter, accept or renounce whose signature is missing, malformed, or does not verify (hosted: against the passport key; local: `session` is required).
- `offer_unknown`: accept, counter or withdraw whose respond_to names no offer visible to the sender.
- `offer_self_accept`: accept or counter of the sender's own offer. The action schema already refuses such a frame (power echo); the engine re-checks it independently (defence in depth) and reports this code if that check ever fires.
- `offer_conflict`: the named offer is no longer live (countered, withdrawn, expired, or already bound). In one round the order of application is withdraw, counter, accept, offer, renounce, so a withdraw beats an accept of the same offer.
- `commitment_unknown`: renounce whose respond_to names no ACTIVE commitment between the sender and the renounce's recipient: an unknown or foreign id, a commitment with another counterparty, one that has ENDED (every clause settled every phase it covers; 2.5.0: refused, never an accepted no-op), or one already renounced (a second renounce, including a second one in the same round, which is refused at the round close). One hint for every cause.
- `terms_invalid`: a clause is out of range: to_phase more than 4 movement phases after from_phase (one clause covers at most 5), from_phase after to_phase, a phase already adjudicated, an order clause for a unit the obligor does not hold at submission, or a no_attack / no_support_against naming the obligor itself.
- `clause_beyond_horizon` (2.5.0): an offer or counter with a clause that covers a movement phase after the game's final one, F<final_year>M (observation `horizon.final_year`; RunSpec `diplomacy.horizon_year`). Such a clause could never settle. Only reachable when final_year is before 1908: a phase after 1908 already fails the action schema (frame-level schema_invalid). Contracts 2.1.0 to 2.4.0 had no code for it, and the wire layers sent `terms_invalid`.
- `asks_invalid`: an asks entry does not parse, or is not an order for a unit of a recipient in the current phase.
- `reply_to_unknown`: reply_to names a message the sender never received or sent.

msg_index.description: 0-based index of the message in the sender's `press` array.

move.description: The move of the rejected message, when it was readable.

code.description: Stable machine code (list above; errors.md §3e). New codes may be added in a MINOR: treat an unknown code as a generic refusal. (2.5.0) `clause_beyond_horizon` added; a client written against 2.4.0 treats it as generic (it was sent as `terms_invalid` before).

hint.description: Fixed, platform-authored explanation for the developer. Never contains the rejected text or hidden state.

round.description: The press round the batch was sent in; absent when the batch was sent outside a round.

tick.description: The tick of the step the batch was submitted in.

phase.description: Any adjudicator phase id: S/F movement or retreat, W adjustment (e.g. S1902M, F1902R, W1902A).

examples.hint: Message body exceeds 600 bytes after sanitisation; it was not delivered. Split or shorten it.
Press is accepted only in press rounds r1..rR of a movement phase; this step was orders.
respond_to names no offer you have received.
respond_to names no active commitment you are a party to.
A clause covers a movement phase after this game's final one; it could never settle.
